finding: For every normal traceless A and every traceless B unitarily reducible into blocks of dimension at most2 (no separate block trace assumption), η(A,B)=σ1(X)²+σ2(X)²≤2L. After A is diagonal and B is in its 2×2 reducing blocks, H=X†X is a direct sum of PSD matrices of size≤2. For any such H, the additive compound modulus has exactly the same top eigenvalue as the original compound: each 2×2 Hermitian block is phase-gaugeable to an entrywise nonnegative one; its within-block wedge is scalar trace and cross-block modulus is the Kronecker sum of the two moduli. Thus f274's η equals actual top-two sum. The accepted one-normal-factor T2 bound then supplies η≤2L; the equality η=S2 itself is independent of T2. B may be nonnormal with B² nonnormal, since its two 2×2 blocks need only have opposite total traces, not zero trace individually.
